# must-i-file Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Must I File 2026: Decide whether a US taxpayer must file a federal income tax return for tax year 2026.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always review when dependent is yes

The app SHALL answer `review` when dependent is yes, because applying adult thresholds to a dependent gives a wrong answer.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 3000 yes no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `review`
- **AND** the app answers `review`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never none when special is yes

The app SHALL NOT answer `none` when special is yes, because self-employment tax, advance premium credits and special taxes must be reported on a return.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `head 0 10000 no yes no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `none`
- **AND** the app answers `file`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never none when payments is yes

The app SHALL NOT answer `none` when payments is yes, because telling someone with tax withheld to skip filing forfeits their refund.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 50000 no no yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `none`
- **AND** the app answers `file`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Always file when status is single and gross is at least 18150 and dependent is no

The app SHALL answer `file` when status is single and gross is at least 18150 and dependent is no, because above the highest single threshold a return is always required.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 50000 no no yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `file`
- **AND** the app answers `file`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Always file when status is joint and gross is at least 35500 and dependent is no

The app SHALL answer `file` when status is joint and gross is at least 35500 and dependent is no, because above the highest joint threshold a return is always required.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `joint 0 35500 no yes yes`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `file`
- **AND** the app answers `file`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never file when gross is below 5 and special is no

The app SHALL NOT answer `file` when gross is below 5 and special is no, because nobody without income or special items is told they must file.

Verified: not proved: see the counterexample (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 0 yes no yes`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `file`
- **AND** the app answers `review`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-001 review when dependent is yes

The app SHALL answer `review` when dependent is yes, because dependents use a different test based on earned and unearned income.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 3000 yes no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `review`, decided by REQ-001

The app SHALL answer `file` when special is yes and no earlier rule matches, because self-employment tax from $400 and these items require a return at any income.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `head 0 10000 no yes no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `file`, decided by REQ-002

The app SHALL answer `file` when status is separate and gross is at least 5 and no earlier rule matches, because married filing separately must file from $5 at any age.

### Requirement: REQ-011 refund when payments is yes

The app SHALL answer `refund` when payments is yes and no earlier rule matches, because only a return gets withheld tax or refundable credits back.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule11`).

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refund`, decided by REQ-011

### Requirement: Otherwise none

The app SHALL answer `none` when no rule matches, because income is under every 2026 threshold and nothing else requires a return.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 15000 no no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `none`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `single 0 50000 no no yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `file`, decided by REQ-004, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `file`, `refund`, `none`, `review`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `single`, `joint`, `separate`, `head` | filing status: single, married filing jointly (also qualifying surviving spouse, whose thresholds are the same), married filing separately, head of household |
| `seniors` | whole number from 0 up to 2 | how many filers on the return are 65 or older at the end of 2026 (born before January 2, 1962) |
| `gross` | whole number from 0 up to 99999999 | gross income for 2026 as IRS Publication 501 defines it, in whole dollars; combined for a joint return |
| `dependent` | `yes`, `no` | whether someone else can claim you as a dependent |
| `special` | `yes`, `no` | whether you had net self-employment earnings of $400 or more, received advance premium tax credit payments, took HSA or Archer MSA distributions, or owe a special tax such as household employment, IRA additional tax, or Social Security tax |
| `payments` | `yes`, `no` | whether tax was withheld or estimated tax paid, or you may qualify for a refundable credit such as the earned income credit |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | you must file a 2026 federal return |
| `refund` | you need not file, but filing may get money back |
| `none` | you need not file a 2026 federal return |
| `review` | dependent thresholds apply; check IRS Publication 501, Table 2 |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- Decides only whether a 2026 federal return is required; it does not compute tax, prepare a return, or file one.
- State returns are not covered.
- Dependents get review: their thresholds depend on earned versus unearned income (IRS Publication 501, Table 2).
- You work out gross income yourself; most Social Security benefits are excluded from it (see Publication 501).
- A qualifying surviving spouse enters joint, because the 2026 thresholds are the same.
- Blindness does not change these filing thresholds, so it is not asked.
- For single and head of household, seniors above 1 counts as 1.
- Married filing separately must file from $5 of gross income at any age.
- Nonresident aliens, dual-status filers and US residents of territories are not covered.
- Thresholds are the 2026 standard deductions from Rev. Proc. 2025-32: $16,100 single, $32,200 joint and surviving spouse, $24,150 head of household, plus $2,050 (single or head) or $1,650 (married) per filer 65 or older.

## Examples

- `single 0 50000 no no yes` gives `file`
- `single 0 15000 no no yes` gives `refund`
- `single 0 15000 no no no` gives `none`
- `single 0 16099 no no no` gives `none`
- `single 0 16100 no no no` gives `file`
- `single 1 17000 no no no` gives `none`
- `joint 2 35000 no no no` gives `none`
- `joint 1 35000 no no no` gives `file`
- `joint 0 32200 no no no` gives `file`
- `separate 0 100 no no no` gives `file`
- `head 0 10000 no yes no` gives `file`
- `head 1 25000 no no no` gives `none`
- `single 0 3000 yes no no` gives `review`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
